content: Aucoumea klaineana Pierre (Okoume, Gabonese mahogany) — Burseraceae. Gabon's dominant commercial species, occurring in semi-deciduous and secondary forests from 0-800 m elevation. Wood density rho = 0.44 g/cm3 (basic density), light pink to reddish, low durability (Class 4-5), excellent peeling quality for plywood. Diameter growth is fast: peak mean annual increment of about 2.26 cm/year at DBH 21 cm (Engone Obiang et al. 2013); trees reach 50-60 cm DBH in 40-50 years on productive sites. Chapman-Richards diameter asymptote A = 75 cm, growth rate k = 0.055/yr, shape p = 1.8. Commercially mature at 55-60 years. Common names FR: Okoume, Okoumé. Grows on ferrallitic soils with 1200-1800 mm rainfall. Height-diameter: H = 1.3 + 42.7 * exp(-1.426/D) approx (Central African moist forest form).

Lophira alata Banks ex Gaertn.f. (Azobe, Red Ironwood) — Ochnaceae. Very heavy hardwood, wood density rho = 1.06 g/cm3, deep red-brown, extremely durable (Class 1-2, highly resistant to marine borers and termites). Slow growth: Chapman-Richards diameter asymptote A = 60 cm, k = 0.032/yr, p = 1.6; peak MAI under 1.0 cm/year. Trees require 80-120+ years to reach commercial 60 cm DBH. Shade-tolerant late-successional species of moist evergreen forest, Gabon/Cameroon basin. Common names FR: Azobe, Bilinga. High shrinkage, hard to season (18-24 months air drying); used for heavy construction, railway sleepers, harbour works.

Pterocarpus soyauxii Taub. (Padouk, African Padauk) — Fabaceae. Wood density rho = 0.75 g/cm3, vivid orange-red heartwood turning brown, durable Class 2. Moderate-fast growth: Chapman-Richards A = 65 cm, k = 0.045/yr, p = 1.7; commercial diameter 50-60 cm reached in 50-70 years. Light-demanding pioneer of gaps and secondary forest, 0-600 m elevation, 1200-2000 mm rainfall. Common names FR: Padouk, Bété. Bark rich in tannins; heartwood extractives used traditionally against fungal infection. Low formaldehyde-free bio-glue potential from bark flavanols.

Perse buxifolia (Ozigo, Whitewood) — Lauraceae (syn. Ocotea usambarensis var. overallii for Gabonese ozigo populations reported in forestry literature). Wood density rho = 0.47 g/cm3, light, pale yellow-brown, moderate durability Class 3-4, used for joinery, matches, plywood. Moderate growth: Chapman-Richards A = 70 cm, k = 0.050/yr, p = 1.75; commercial 50 cm DBH in 35-45 years. Common names FR: Ozigo. Occurs in moist evergreen lowland forest, Gabon basin; secondary successional. Fast recovery after disturbance makes it suitable for reduced-impact logging (EFIR) rotations.

Baillonella toxisperma Pierre (Moabi, Djave) — Sapotaceae. Wood density rho = 0.83 g/cm3, pink-brown, durable Class 2, heavy hardwood. Slow growth: Chapman-Richards A = 62 cm, k = 0.035/yr, p = 1.65; commercial 60 cm DBH in 80-100 years. Large emergent tree (40-50 m) of undisturbed evergreen forest; animal-dispersed seeds; slow regeneration, vulnerable to over-exploitation — protected under Gabonese forest law with exploitation quotas. Common names FR: Moabi. Kernel fat (moabi butter) used in food and cosmetics. Biodiversity indicator: presence of large Moabi signals intact forest.
